editorial.headline: Ornamental Plant Retail: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Retail sales of pots and growing media are nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration for this activity.
editorial.body:
**For a foreign investor, this is not a Bali registration opportunity today.** The activity is nationally marked TERBUKA for PMA and carries a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. Yet the Bali entry is unequivocal: it is blocked for PMA registration. That is the central fact for a founder weighing location. National openness defines the position beyond the provincial restriction; it does not itself make a PMA registration available on the island. It is the primary planning distinction in this record, rather than a secondary qualification to be noted later.

The commercial focus is tightly drawn: retail trade in the supplies and media used for ornamental plants, including pots and growing media. The scope also explicitly includes direct sales. In plain English, this is a retail activity for the practical articles that accompany ornamental planting, with the sale of those articles—not a broad label for unrelated activity—at its core. The record names the examples rather than leaving the activity as an abstract category, giving pots and growing media particular weight in its account of the retail offer. The language points to a business whose offer centres on these supplies, served through retail and direct-sale channels.

The listed company scales are Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The record therefore admits the activity at every one of those named scales, from Mikro through Besar, without changing its stated retail subject. That scale coverage matters in reading the entry correctly: the same basic activity is described in one place, while the Bali outcome is assessed separately through its risk-based provincial rule. Direct sales remain expressly in scope alongside the retail description. The scale labels are stated plainly and do not alter the named subject of the activity.

Bali is the decisive constraint. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is recorded as Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope. Bali’s rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration, island-wide and permanently; for this activity, the record specifically ties the block to the Bali moratorium of 13 May 2026. A 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling is thus a national fact, not a Bali availability statement. It cannot be treated as permission to register a PMA for this activity in Bali while the provincial block stated in the record applies. This is why the national and Bali fields must be read together, without allowing one to erase the other.
editorial.pullQuote: A 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling is a national fact, not a Bali availability statement.
